title: Thyme-infused oil for muscle rub
subtitle: A warming massage oil of Thymus vulgaris in olive oil for tight, sore muscles
excerpt: Thyme-infused oil is dried thyme herb slow-infused in olive oil for 4 to 6 weeks, then strained and bottled for use as a warming muscle rub. A traditional external preparation, applied to tight, sore back muscles, stiff necks, and areas of muscular tension. The thymol in thyme oil is both warming and mildly antimicrobial. Makes 100 ml; keeps 12 months in a dark glass bottle.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), thyme entry, Botanical.com. Cold maceration method for herbal oils documented in: Hoffman, D., Medical Herbalism (2003), in the public domain summary of traditional preparations. Historical European herbalists' use of thyme as an external warming preparation: Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653).

recipe.yieldDescription: 100 ml infused oil (approx. 15 to 20 massage applications)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Infuse 4 to 6 weeks. Keeps 12 months in a dark glass bottle. Batch doubling: scale herb and oil proportionally.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of making an infused oil by submerging dried herb in oil at room temperature for several weeks, rather than applying heat. Slower than a warm infusion but preserves heat-sensitive constituents and is less likely to cause rancidity.

for 4 to 6 weeks, then strained into a dark glass bottle for use as a warming muscle rub. The thymol and carvacrol extracted from the herb into the oil give it a gentle warming, rubefacient action on the skin, applied with firm massage to tight back muscles, stiff necks, or areas of chronic muscular tension. The oil has a strong, clean, herbal scent from the thyme's volatile components. A 10 to 15 minute massage with the warmed oil.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried thyme, must be fully dried, not fresh
light olive oil or refined olive oil

content.text: Place 30 g of dried thyme in a clean dry glass jar. Pour 200 ml of olive oil over the herb, ensuring the herb is fully submerged. If any herb floats above the oil surface, press it down and add a little more oil.
Seal the jar and place on a sunny windowsill or in a warm spot (not direct heat) for 4 to 6 weeks. Turn the jar daily.
After 4 to 6 weeks, strain through muslin into a dark glass bottle, pressing the herb to extract the oil. The finished oil will be a warm yellow-green with a distinct thyme scent.
Label with the herb, oil, and date. To use: warm a small amount in the palm of your hand, then massage firmly into the affected area for 10 to 15 minutes.

Apply 1 to 2 teaspoons per massage session. Use once or twice daily for acute soreness, or as needed for ongoing muscular tension. Allow the oil to absorb into the skin for 15 minutes before clothing.
Sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps 12 months. Discard if the oil smells rancid.
When not to use this remedy

Do not apply to broken skin. See a doctor for muscle pain that is severe or unexplained. Also see a doctor for pain that comes with weakness, nerve symptoms, or follows an injury. These need assessment before any external treatment.
